decision: retain: approximately 60% less common-name build/update peak memory; modest cold-build and rename gains, no single-edit speedup; unchanged-sync slowdown did not reproduce

performance.interpretation: Retained for bounded dependency representation and repeated 59–64% lower common-name peak RSS. Median cold graph improved 5.1%, rename 10.5%, deletion 1.2%, while edit was 0.7% slower. Sparse edit was 0.6% slower. Three-sample timing variance is substantial: no broad latency claim. An additional seven measured unchanged calls per arm/corpus (plus warmups) found baseline/candidate medians 1.354/1.335s sparse and 1.372/1.305s common, with identical graphs. The initial unchanged slowdown did not reproduce. RSS comparisons use matching arms within the same experiment, not across control harness runs.

results.correctness: Exact generated topology and source hashes, plus identical canonical graph data across every arm/sample; only extraction_run work counters and persistence timestamps are excluded
results.limitations: Synthetic Python local calls; no mixed-language or cross-repository completeness claim. Cold graph excludes initial source admission and passage indexing.
results.method: Alternating arm order; identical admitted seed restored at the same path per arm/sample; fresh CLI processes and warm OS cache; cold graph then unchanged/edit/rename/delete; setup excluded; process peak RSS
